article.name: Hippo
article.summary: Hippo is a local-first memory system for coding agents, with a SQLite store, CLI/API/MCP integrations, tenant and project boundaries, lexical and optional vector retrieval, and lifecycle operations for superseding, forgetting, and maintaining memories. This review describes the current source at the verified upstream head; it is not a runtime or benchmark result.

contact.note: The official pinned README and official project homepage were checked; neither publishes a contact email. No profile or commit metadata, third-party directory, or inferred address was used.

who_what.text: The official README presents Hippo as a local-first memory tool for coding agents, with a CLI and integrations for agent hooks, plugins, and MCP clients. It also describes a team server that exposes a shared store through tenant-bound API keys and roles.

The reviewed implementation stores memory entries in SQLite and separates API/domain logic, store adapters, and CLI/MCP/HTTP surfaces; the repository also contains adjacent continuity, connector, and graph features beyond the memory-entry paths inspected here.

architecture.text: A memory entry carries text plus lifecycle and retrieval metadata: kind, layer, tags, strength and half-life, confidence, timestamps, outcome counters, optional scope/owner, tenant ID and project origin. Provenance-related fields include source, artifact reference, source session ID, lead-in, extraction origin, parents, and supersession successor.

The write API validates caller scope and ownership, screens new content for secrets and instruction-like text, creates a typed entry, then hands it to a SQLite store adapter. The adapter persists rows and keeps full-text and vector indexes synchronized; mutation and recall paths can append audit events.

Recall loads a bounded candidate pool from the tenant store, applying scope and project filters before scoring. The ranker can combine BM25 with vector cosine using a weighted blend or reciprocal-rank fusion; strength and recency affect ranking, and optional stages include graph expansion, MMR, reranking, and a result-token budget.

behavior.text: Writes default to distilled memories; callers can set kind, layer, confidence, tags, scope, owner, artifact reference, lead-in and project identity. The shared remember path vets secret-like material and screens shared-member or connector text for instruction-like patterns. Where the store supports review, flagged writes can be held in quarantine; these source checks do not show that every unsafe input is detected.

A memory can be corrected with supersede: a successor is stored and linked to the old memory, with an audit event; default recall excludes superseded entries. This preserves a correction chain instead of replacing old text in place.

Forget requires the caller to reach and have write rights to the row. It removes a non-raw row from SQLite and full-text search, records the operation, and attempts mirror cleanup after commit. Raw transcript rows are append-only through ordinary forget and use a separate archive path. The rejection guard stores a tenant-scoped digest and reason, not rejected content, and blocks exact normalized text re-ingestion; semantic paraphrases are outside the guard.

Recall applies tenant identity from the authenticated context and passes scope and project-origin filters into candidate loading before the ranking window. Superseded rows are excluded by default. Search combines BM25 with optional vector similarity; optional stages include graph expansion, diversity reranking, configured rerankers and a token budget.

SQLite FTS5 and trigram tables provide lexical candidate indexes; memory vectors are stored as Float32 blobs. Failed FTS synchronization marks the index out of sync and emits a warning, leaving SQLite rows authoritative but potentially reducing recall until repair.

The API audit log records tenant, actor, operation, target, timestamp and metadata. Recall audit metadata hashes the query rather than persisting its text. Operational events do not establish quality or performance.

metrics.evidence: The inspected recall pipeline ranks lexical and optional vector candidates under scope and a result budget; no answerability or abstention workload was scored.
Supersession preserves a successor link and default recall excludes superseded rows; no correction probes were run.
Forget deletes a row and synchronizes indexes/mirrors, while raw rows have an archive path; no post-delete leakage probes were run.
Tenant, caller scope, and project-origin filters are applied to candidate loading; whole-store sleep is cross-tenant, and no isolation workload was run.
Memory metadata can retain source, artifact reference, lead-in, source session, and extraction/parent links; no recalled claim was adjudicated against source passages.
No runtime timings or write-to-recall intervals were collected.
SQLite indexes and optional local vectors were inspected; no token, cost, storage-size, or workload measurements were collected.

limits.text: Tenant and project boundaries depend on the store and surface supplying the intended authenticated context; CLI/operator routes and background whole-store sleep have different reach from an API caller. Sleep explicitly processes all tenants, and its source comments describe a loopback-only boundary. No cross-tenant or cross-project isolation probes were run.

Confidence labels, source labels, counts and artifact references are stored metadata; the reviewed paths do not validate that a source passage entails a memory or that repeated observations are independent. A digest tombstone rejects matching normalized text, not paraphrases.
Forget and archive paths were inspected, but complete erasure from backups and every derivative copy was not established. This review did not trace every connector-specific retention path.

The repository README includes product descriptions and upstream evaluation claims, but this review did not reproduce those results. The current homepage shows a different displayed version from the repository head; implementation claims here use the pinned source review.

benchmark.note: No Hippo runtime, tests, or benchmark workload was run. Code observations and project evaluation definitions are not Hippo benchmark results.
